comparisons.peer_topic: Income Tax Provision and Effective Rates
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company recorded an income tax provision of $381 million and an income tax benefit of $346 million in 2024 and 2023, with effective tax rates of 19% and (68%) respectively, driven by higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose specific non-recurring or structural drivers for their income tax provision changes. AVGO attributes its 2024 provision increase to a non-recurring intra-group transfer of IP rights to the U.S., whereas AMD attributes its increase to a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction alongside higher pre-tax income. While both cite structural transactions impacting the tax provision, the specific nature differs (IP transfer vs. integration transaction), and AMD also highlights a significant effective tax rate swing compared to AVGO's focus on provision magnitude.

sentences.text: The increase in provision for income taxes in fiscal year 2024 compared to fiscal year 2023 was primarily due to the impact of a non-recurring intra-group transfer of certain IP rights to the United States as a result of supply chain realignment and the resulting shift in jurisdictional mix of income, partially offset by an increase in excess tax benefits from stock-based awards.
The increase in income tax provision in 2024 was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and a $373 million tax effect from an intercompany integration transaction.

peer_results.rationale: INTC candidates focus on balance sheet line items (receivables/payables) and R&D credit methodology rather than the drivers of the income tax provision or effective rate changes comparable to AVGO's disclosure of non-recurring IP transfers and pre-tax income impacts.

MU candidates focus on share-based award tax benefits and the materiality of tax incentive arrangements, which are distinct from AVGO's disclosure of the primary drivers of the aggregate income tax provision (IP transfer and pre-tax income).

NVDA candidates provided are either unrelated geographic revenue data or accounting policies for interest/penalties, lacking substantive comparison to AVGO's disclosure of the drivers for the income tax provision amount.
